title: Quality checks
purpose: Our own team watches every video before the client sees it. Bad footage stops here. The person who made it hears about it within 24 hours.
how: This is the daily audit. A KMSC reviewer watches every video the next day, before the client sees it, and marks it keep, flag, or delete. A keep can come with feedback. Youssef Medhat leads the team and reports to Youssif. Reviewers work remotely all day on the footage from the day before, five for every 1,000 hours a day.

In the daily audit the reviewer checks four things in order: angle, lighting, movement, then the eight fraud patterns. Angle means the camera sees what the worker's eyes see. Movement means real work for the whole cycle. The patterns are the cards below. Every wearer signed off on them at onboarding screening, so a flag is never a surprise.

A flag comes from us. A strike comes from the client. A flag reaches the Portfolio Manager the same day, and Moharam gets an alert within the hour. The Portfolio Manager tells the worker within 24 hours with a specific correction: not 'be careful' but 'the camera was on your chest, it goes on the hat'. The wearer log names who wore the phone, so the flag goes on the person, not the phone.

breaks.what: The client gives a strike to an account we passed as clean
breaks.do: This is the number that matters most. Youssef Medhat opens the session, finds out why it passed, and watches it again with the reviewer the same day. The session joins the calibration set. Youssif is told about each one. The worker still gets the correction within 24 hours.

breaks.what: Footage arrives faster than the reviewers can watch it
breaks.do: Unreviewed footage is a backlog. Youssef Medhat owns it the same day and tells Youssif. Mano starts hiring more reviewers, five for every 1,000 hours a day. We never send unreviewed footage to the client to reach a target.

breaks.what: A worker says a flag is wrong
breaks.do: The Portfolio Manager sends Youssef Medhat the session ID, the account, what the flag says, and what the worker says happened. He watches the session again and answers the same day. His decision is final. Only Youssif can change it.

breaks.what: The same pattern shows up across a whole site
breaks.do: This is not ten bad workers. It is one failed briefing or one wrong rig. The Portfolio Manager briefs the whole site again before the next shift. If the mount is the problem, Ali gets photos and a rig count the same day.

breaks.what: A worker reaches three flags, but the site needs the hours
breaks.do: The worker is removed anyway. Someone from the 10% trained bench takes the phone in the same shift. Hours from a flagged worker do not count. That footage is deleted later.

questions.q: My video was rated "Great". How can it be fraud?
questions.a: The rating is a score in the collection app. The fraud check is separate. Videos rated Great have been flagged before. Only real work with the camera on your head protects you.

questions.q: Who sees the video first, us or the client?
questions.a: We do. Every video, every time. That is why the team exists.

questions.q: What is the difference between a flag and a strike?
questions.a: A flag comes from us: our reviewer caught the problem first. A strike comes from the client: they caught it. Three flags remove the worker from the project. Two strikes pause the phone. We want zero strikes and every problem caught as a flag.

questions.q: The worker says the mount slipped. Does the flag still count?
questions.a: The footage is deleted either way. Youssef Medhat decides if the flag counts against the worker, after the Portfolio Manager sends him what the worker says happened. A slipped mount is refitted before the next cycle. If it keeps slipping, Ali is told.

funnel.text: Everything that arrives from the collection app. Nothing here is accepted yet.
The daily audit. A KMSC reviewer watches every video the next day and checks angle, lighting, movement, and the eight patterns.
Clean footage. It goes to the client. These are the accepted hours, and everyone is paid on them.
Kept, but the worker gets a correction within 24 hours: the angle moved, the lighting was dim, or the cycle ended early. Not fraud, but it must be fixed.
A fraud pattern matched. The flag goes on the person in the wearer log. The penalty is in the handbook. Three of these remove the worker from the project.
Flagged footage, and any footage that must not exist. It is never sent and never invoiced.

patterns.name: Idle recording
patterns.what: The worker sits or stands still, or the phone is mounted somewhere, and no real work happens.
patterns.tell: The picture barely changes for minutes. No hands in view. Same wall, same angle.
patterns.fix: Tap stop the moment work stops. Never record breaks, waiting, or talking.

patterns.name: Hat off while recording
patterns.what: The worker takes the rig off and the phone keeps recording.
patterns.tell: Ceiling, sky, a tabletop, or the inside of a bag. The video often ends with a face.
patterns.fix: Tap stop before you take the hat off. Button first, then hat.

patterns.name: Camera pointed at the body or the floor
patterns.what: The phone is on the head but tilted down. It films the floor or the worker's own body.
patterns.tell: The worker's torso and the floor fill the picture. Hands show only at the top edge. The task is out of view.
patterns.fix: Check the angle every time you restart recording. The camera must see what your eyes see. The operator checks it on every sweep.

patterns.name: Chest mount
patterns.what: The phone is clipped to a pocket or a strap, not to the hat.
patterns.tell: The picture is low and steady and does not turn when the worker looks around. Arms come in from the sides.
patterns.fix: The mount goes on the hat or the certified helmet, nowhere else. The client's system counts a chest mount as fraud, comfortable or not.

patterns.name: Filming someone else
patterns.what: The camera points at another worker doing the work while the wearer only watches.
patterns.tell: A whole person is in the picture doing the task. The wearer's own hands never appear.
patterns.fix: Film your own hands doing your own work. When your task is done, tap stop.

patterns.name: Fake tasks
patterns.what: Wiping a clean surface. Moving boxes back and forth. Sweeping a floor with no dirt.
patterns.tell: The same task repeats and nothing changes. Nothing gets dirtier, cleaner, fuller, or emptier.
patterns.fix: Record real work only. If you have no work, tap stop, tell the operator, and take the rig off.

patterns.name: Filming a screen
patterns.what: The worker films a screen playing old footage, or feeds an old session into the app again.
patterns.tell: A framed rectangle, flicker, or moving bands. Timestamps do not match the shift.
patterns.fix: No fix. This is on purpose. The worker is fired at once, as the handbook says, and the account is closed.

patterns.name: The same problem after a correction
patterns.what: The same worker repeats the same pattern after the Portfolio Manager gave the correction.
patterns.tell: The watchlist shows it. Youssef Medhat checks every flag against the account's history.
patterns.fix: Two corrections is the limit. The third flag removes the worker from the project.

rules.name: Three flags
rules.text: Three flags on one account remove the worker from the project. The account is closed for good. The worker is never enrolled again, under any name or on any phone. Fakes made on purpose do not wait for three flags: looped footage, a covered lens, or a recorded screen means the worker is fired at once, as the handbook says.

rules.name: Second strike
rules.text: A strike comes from the client. On the second strike on one account, the phone pauses by itself and Moharam is told within the hour. It stays paused until the worker gets the fraud briefing again and the operator signs off again.

rules.name: 24 hours
rules.text: A flag reaches the Portfolio Manager the same day it is raised. The worker hears about it within 24 hours, in person at the site, with the video open and a specific correction. The flag closes when the fix is seen in the next cycle, not when the message is sent.

rules.name: Second pass at month end
rules.text: In the last week of the month, Youssef Medhat runs a second pass over the whole month's footage, after the daily audits. Flagged footage is deleted. Payouts go out on that number, then the invoice to the client, on accepted hours only.
